html:
On 15 January 2022 the undersea volcano Hunga Tonga erupted north of Tongatapu in the most powerful explosion recorded by modern instruments. Its pressure wave circled the Earth several times and its plume reached higher than any on record.

A tsunami swept the coasts of Tonga and crossed the Pacific, causing damage as far away as Peru. Ash covered Tongatapu, and the only undersea internet cable was cut, leaving Tonga largely cut off for weeks.

The blast also threw a huge mass of water vapour into the upper atmosphere. Like Tambora and Krakatoa before it, it gave scientists a new case for how eruptions reach the whole planet.
